A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study, On Pruning State-Space LLMs. Their methods, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and can be matched across restructuring and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original pruning experiments on four SSM-based models, six benchmark tasks, a loss-function comparison, and projection-component sensitivity measurements.

after.justification: V2 retains those original experiments and adds higher-sparsity results, inference-throughput measurements, a transformer comparison, and LLAMBA-1B evaluations.

M1.justification: WANDA, Taylor-based state and head-dimension pruning, mean-pooled head merging, and SSM-FLAP retain their procedures. Knowledge-distillation fine-tuning is also unchanged; the additional experiments introduce no new method component.

E1.justification: Both versions use WikiText2 and the same six benchmarks: LAMBADA, HellaSwag, PIQA, ARC-Easy, ARC-Challenge, and WinoGrande. Added model configurations, sparsity levels, and timing measurements do not introduce new datasets or language-task coverage.

E2.justification: Appendix D and Figure 7 add transformer-based Smol17 (TF) as an evaluated comparator to Smol-Mamba-1.9B under WANDA. The original pruning-method comparisons remain unchanged. Table 11 itself contains only Mamba rows, but Figure 7 explicitly includes transformer results.

E3.justification: V2 adds 60–90% WANDA sparsity settings, LLAMBA-1B evaluations, and throughput measurements across batch sizes 1, 4, and 16 and sequence lengths 128, 512, and 1024. These extend the experimental settings; the original evaluation and fine-tuning protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 substantially expands the analyses: Table 3 investigates WANDA's high-sparsity failure boundary, Appendix D/Figure 7 compares transformer and Mamba pruning sensitivity, and Table 12 tests whether structured pruning produces runtime gains. The earlier loss-choice and projection-sensitivity analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. V2's additional experiments continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Original Tables 1–2 and v1 Tables 3–9 retain their values, with the latter becoming v2 Tables 4–10. Substantial new results include Smol-Mamba average accuracy falling from 0.485 at 70% sparsity to 0.384 at 80%, throughput measurements, transformer comparisons, and LLAMBA-1B scores. These are additional results, not improvements over matched v1 settings.

T1.justification: The SSM tensor definitions and mathematical architectural descriptions are unchanged. Neither version contains theoretical propositions or proofs that are added, removed, or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contribution and headline claims: SSM pruning feasibility depends strongly on the method, WANDA and state pruning are comparatively robust, and head/output-projection pruning is more damaging. The added experiments do not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: Appendix D adds interpretations about transformer versus Mamba tolerance, practical FLAP acceleration, and sparse-kernel overhead under memory-bandwidth constraints. Section 4 emphasizes OutProj sensitivity despite its smaller parameter count. The original limitations concerning model confounds and SSM-only pruning remain.

D1.justification: V2 documents the new timing hardware: an NVIDIA A100-40GB with 128 GB host RAM and 128 CPU cores. Appendix B's training hyperparameters and A100-80GB setup remain unchanged, as do the code and released-model references.

R1.justification: V2 adds Bick et al. (2025), Llamba: Scaling distilled recurrent models for efficient language processing, and identifies it as concurrent work motivating additional evaluations. The broader research positioning and earlier citations are retained.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized wording and grammar edits, collapses the structured/unstructured method subsection headings, incorporates Results into Experiments, and adds Appendices D and E. Most existing prose and the overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: V2 substantially expands the visual presentation with a radar-plot appendix, Figures 3–10, and tables for higher sparsity, throughput, and additional comparisons. Most radar plots redisplay existing results. Original tables are rearranged, and Figure 2's caption and presentation are simplified.

improvement.justification: The sparsity-boundary test, direct throughput measurements, and additional model comparisons modestly improve the evidence available to assess pruning limits and practical tradeoffs. Reporting problems limit the gain: Appendix D calls FLAP accuracy-preserving despite Table 1's Smol-Mamba accuracy drop from 0.61 to 0.41 at 50% pruning, and its stated 5–17% speedup range omits Table 12's 0.99× case. The added measurements remain useful, but their interpretations require qualification.
